gaps.criterion: Mid-saga crash resumes without duplicating any downstream artifact
gaps.gap: The BEHAVIOUR is implemented and executably proven: saga.ts reads the step ledger back when it finds a claimed run still in 'running' and skips completed steps, and closedWonEscalation.test.ts drives a saga to a throw, forces the run row back to 'running' to reproduce what a killed process actually leaves, then re-runs and asserts the pre-crash step counters are still 1. What is MISSING is endpoint-level proof: neither POST /api/leadflow/closed-won/start nor GET /api/leadflow/sagas/{run_id} has a happy-path api_definition testCase, because the runner has exactly ONE identity (register then login, local role `user` -> sales_rep) and onboarding.manage is held by client_success alone, so every runner call stops at 403. Both definitions therefore prove only the auth/authz surface. Closing this needs a SECOND seeded identity in the shared auth fixtures - a change to tests/api_definitions/auth/*, not to these endpoints - after which a happy-path testCase can call start twice with the same dealId+chargeId and assert `replayed` on the second.
